subject.title: fix(cron): pass allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent from cron executor for both runner paths

question: Should clean empty assistant output be treated as successful silent output for all isolated cron agent runs in both CLI and embedded runner paths?
rationale: The implementation is narrow, but it changes upgrade semantics for cron jobs that currently surface `empty_response` as a failure signal and overlaps with an active adjacent PR that wants delivery-requested genuinely empty completions to error by default.

options.title: Accept all-cron silent success
options.body: Merge this executor-boundary fix and make clean empty assistant output an `ok` silent result for isolated cron runs in both runner paths.

options.title: Require gated silence
options.body: Ask for a revision that only sets the flag for no-deliver, explicit silent, or per-job opted-in cron runs, with tests for default failure and opt-in success.

options.title: Pause for policy consolidation
options.body: Hold this PR while maintainers reconcile it with the adjacent delivery-requested empty-completion policy before choosing a landing branch.

recommendation.title: Accept all-cron silent success
recommendation.body: Merge this executor-boundary fix and make clean empty assistant output an `ok` silent result for isolated cron runs in both runner paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice centers on cron executor policy and runner handoff behavior, where the sampled history points most strongly to this owner route.
